paragraphs.source_en: Conversion and apostasy became more a question of political authority than of religion or theology. Loyalty was tied to religion, which became nationalised.” If a Muslim converted to Christianity, the regime assumed that the apostate would be a fifth column supporting foreign powers. The empire assumed that only Muslims could be loyal to the state, despite its claims to embrace all of its subjects as equals.
